newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight falls to 5.8 pct on big bank lending.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight falls to 5.8 pct on big bank lending.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 5.8/6.0 percent from 7.30/40 percent on Monday on lending by large local banks, dealers said on Tuesday.
However, the overnight was supported by an agent bank of Bank Negara from falling below 5.8 percent, widely accepted as the central bank's floor rate.
"I think Bank Negara is supporting at 5.80 through its agent," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
No confirmation was available as the central bank does not comment on its money market operations.
Dealers said the overnight rate also fell as banks kept funds for payment of a 30-day Bank Negara bill issue on Wednesday.
The issue is to roll over maturing bills of the same amount. The maturity is on Friday.

The central bank earlier announced that it accepted bids for the bill issue at an average yield of 6.296 percent, against 6.959 percent at the previous auction of 30-day bills amounting to 500 million ringgit on April 22.
In the morning, interbank rates were little changed with activity confined to one-month money.
One-week money was at 6.80/90 percent against 6.9/7.0 on Monday, while two-week and three-week were steady at 7.00/10 and 7.10/20 percent respectively.
One-month money was at 7.30/35 percent against 7.25/30, while three-month at 7.35/40 percent and six-month at 7.40/45 were both unchanged.
Dealers said they expected rates to hover at current levels with players continuing to await announcement of a new long-term government bond issue.
Speculation has been rife that Bank Negara will issue new Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) to roll over maturing bonds. A 900-million ringgit issue will mature on May 15.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were marginally lower across the board.
At 0900 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June, September and December contracts were all down one point to 92.68, or an implied yield of 7.32 percent.
March and June 1998 were down two to 92.62, or 7.38 percent.
